sources.excerpt: EarthQuaker Devices Info Email Search Menu EarthQuaker Devices Info Email Search Devices Dealers Blog About Studios OnomatoPedal Merch Small Signal Shredder Plumes® Small Signal Shredder 1. Level: This controls the output volume. 2. Gain: This controls the amount of drive. 3. Tone: More bass to the left, more middles in the middle and more treble to the right. 4. Clipping Modes (3-Way Toggle): 1. Symmetrical LED clipping - More Crunch and Compression. 2. No clipping - Wide open OpAmp drive for clean boost. 3. Asymmetrical silicon diode clipping - More transparency with a loose feel. Plumes is an overdrive based around that classically overdone tube-like circuit you all know, and amps crave. While this particular circuit has been done to death, we here at EarthQuaker Devices brand of special effects pedals think the Plumes offers an original take on the old, tired dead horse everyone loves to beat on. You can’t get enough of it, so we are giving you some more. Doctor’s orders and what not… For starters, we’ve done away with the sacred 4558 IC and the classic BJT transistor buffers and replaced them with JFET operational amplifiers and raised the input impedance to nearly 10 megaohms! This offers lower noise, better signal integrity and more chime in the high end. We power this OpAmp by taking the 9v input and internally converting it to +/- 9v to give it more headroom. The end result is a more three-dimensional tone with added clarity that really pushes a nice tube amp over the edge. You might notice how those badass leads you’re always ripping will blast over those awful, no good cymbals your drummer is constantly bashing around on. It sounds like diamonds … a million f**king diamonds! We’ve also added three different clipping options for your consideration. Mode 1 is symmetrical clipping utilizing a pair of light emitting diodes. This is the crunchiest setting the Plumes has to offer. When played through a clean amp, it’ll deliver a reasonable facsimile of that classic black and gold British valve amp tone. If you already set your amp dirty, using this mode will make it filthy. Mode 2 is clean boost mode. This eliminates the soft clipping diodes altogether and leaves you with straight OpAmp drive. This is perfect for pushing your clean tone out in front or driving the preamp of an already overdriven amp into tasteful breakup territory. Mode 3 is an asymmetrical silicon diode arrangement similar to the stock screamer but with more output and clean clarity; the tone some people describe as “transparent.” It’s almost as if your clean tone is blended in with a slightly less clean tone, ya know? Using this mode gives a warmer low-end response and lower output. It’s less hard on your amp and your ears. It’s a classic pleasant tone the whole band can enjoy. Not enough for you? We’ve also improved the way the classic Tone control operates while still leaving it familiar enough to keep you warm and comfortable. It’s still a safe space, no worries in here. It’s now useful through the whole range. The low end is big and clear, and the high end is bright and cutting without killing the mids. Just the right amount of tonal tickling to excite those ear drums yet still give that familiar mid-heavy drive. GUITAR SAMPLES Blues Lawyer Gibson Les Paul

sources.h1: The Overdrive That Broke the Script: EarthQuaker Devices Plumes Small Signal Shredder
sources.excerpt: EarthQuaker Devices Plumes: three clipping modes and JFET internals make a Tube Screamer upgrade for $99. Specs, tones, and confirmed player guide. admin 22 September 2026 16 min read GG-ARTICLE-TOP Akron, Ohio doesn’t have a coastline or a legendary studio district, but for a certain breed of guitar obsessive, it has something better: EarthQuaker Devices. And the Plumes is the pedal that turned a cult brand into a household name — without selling out a single quirk. GG-ARTICLE-AFTER-INTRO How to Get the Tone ↓ In the Beginning: A Dead Horse Worth Beating Again By 2019, the world did not need another Tube Screamer derivative. The format had been dissected, cloned, modded, and eulogized roughly ten thousand times over. The JRC4558 op-amp had more tribute acts than the Rolling Stones. So when EarthQuaker Devices founder Jamie Stillman sat down to design a TS-style overdrive for his catalog, he could have coasted. He didn’t. The Plumes Small Signal Shredder was unveiled at Summer NAMM 2019 and hit store shelves on August 3rd of that year. EarthQuaker’s own product copy is typically self-deprecating: “You can’t get enough of it, so we are giving you some more. Doctor’s orders and what not.” The copy sold itself short. Sweetwater named it a hot pick, Premier Guitar handed it a Premier Gear Award, and within months it was one of the fastest-moving EQD products ever. Guitarists who had spent years avoiding yet another screamer were buying it by the handful. The reason? Stillman tore out the canonical guts of the circuit and replaced them with something better. Out went the sacred JRC4558 IC and the bipolar transistor buffers that every other screamer uses. In came JFET operational amplifiers — field-effect transistors in the op-amp stage — and input impedance raised to nearly ten megaohms. On paper that’s an engineering detail. In practice it means less noise, better signal integrity, more chime at the top end, and a low-end response that doesn’t vanish into the circuit the way a classic 4558-based screamer’s can. There’s also a power trick inside the box: the Plumes takes your standard 9-volt supply and internally converts it to plus/minus 9 volts, giving the op-amp a full 18-volt rail to breathe on. That’s the headroom story — and it’s a real one. Where vintage screamer clones can compress and flatten when you dig in hard, the Plumes opens up. EarthQuaker calls it “almost three-dimensional clarity.” That’s marketing language, but this particular marketing language is accurate. Physically, the Plumes arrived in EQD’s standard compact enclosure: 4.75 by 2.50 by 2.25 inches, festooned with the hand-drawn artwork that’s been a studio signature since Stillman started building pedals out of his living room in the mid-2000s. EarthQuaker grew from a one-person operation to a proper factory in Akron, Ohio — still hand-wired, still weird, still proudly midwestern — and the Plumes represents that lineage in concentrated form. Specs at a Glance Key Specifications Type Analog overdrive / clean boost Release Date August 3, 2019 (announced Summer NAMM 2019) Controls Level, Gain, Tone + 3-way clipping mode toggle Clipping Modes 1: Symmetrical LED; 2: No clipping (clean boost); 3: Asymmetrical silicon Op-Amp JFET (replaces JRC4558) Input Impedance ~10 MΩ Output Impedance 100 Ω Internal Voltage ±9V (converted from 9VDC input) Switching Flexi-Switch® relay-based true bypass (momentary + latching) Current Draw 25 mA Power 9VDC center-negative (no battery; DO NOT run at higher voltages) Dimensions 4.75″ × 2.50″ × 2.25″ (121 × 64 × 57 mm) with knobs Street Price ~$99 new; ~$55–70 used Made Akron, Ohio, USA Warranty Limited lifetime One important caveat before the controls section: unlike EQD’s previous overdrive designs and unlike many boutique drives that benefit from running at 18 volts, the Plumes must not be run at higher voltages. The internal doubling circuit is already doing that work — feed it 18V externally and you risk damage. Nine volts only. The Three Clipping Modes: A Closer Look The Plumes’ three-way toggle is the controlling idea of the whole pedal. Most TS-style drives offer one voicing; the Plumes offers three distinct characters, and the differences are more than cosmetic. Mode 1 — Symmetrical LED Clipping This is the crunchiest option. A matched pair of light-emitting diodes handle the clipping symmetrically on both the positive and negative waveform halves. The result is tighter, more compressed, and more harmonically aggressive than the other modes. Through a clean amp it can approximate a British valve amp pushed into saturation — think more Marshall-adjacent, less Fender-adjacent. Through an already dirty amp, Mode 1 gets genuinely filthy in a useful, controllable way. Mode 2 — No Clipping (Clean Boost) Remove the diodes entirely and you have pure op-amp drive with nothing to clip the signal. Mode 2 is the Plumes in clean boost territory: big, open, and thunderously loud at high Level settings. It’s ideal for pushing an amp’s own preamp into breakup — the Plumes’ JFET circuit preserves the character of whatever comes after it rather than coloring it. This mode works especially well stacked after another overdrive, where it acts as a level boost without adding its own saturation character. Mode 3 — Asymmetrical Silicon Diode Clipping This is the mode closest to the original Tube Screamer topology: one silicon diode clips the positive half while another handles the negative half, but they’re arranged asymmetrically. Asymmetrical clipping produces even-order harmonics alongside the odd-order components — the same principle that makes tube amps sound warm rather than harsh. In practice Mode 3 delivers more transparency, a looser feel, a warmer low-end response, and slightly lower output than Mode 1.
